rows.what the ink shows: A low opening cluster and two taller middle strokes remain, but the heavy cancellation runs through almost the entire letter body; the internal sequence cannot be securely separated.

The first word has a descending p, crossed t and long descending q; the following low word and separate looped l-group support “seule la”. The final word retains its open c, upright middle strokes and low extended ending beneath the cancellation.
An open c is followed by a low ons sequence, a dotted i and a tall looped d; the separated small accent and successive low strokes continue through the final ra.
The opening rounded a and low une remain under the strike; the last group has a dotted initial i, a central d rise, a separate accent, tall final t and terminal point.

The final q has a deep descending return followed by a low u and short apostrophe stroke. The initial horizontal loop is crowded by the adjacent long curved line and does not separate the proposed lors letters.
The insertion begins with an open c and flattened on, followed by an upright crossed t; a small e turn and joined low nu finish the word.
A low left hook turns into a horizontal rightward arm before the clearly parenthesized A. The diagonal deletion crosses the hook and prevents deciding whether it closes as sigma or is an r shoulder.
The prefix has a top arm extending right and a small curved remnant below it, followed by (A). Its left joint lies under the diagonal deletion, leaving sigma and r unresolved.
The tall initial S, low u and two adjacent p descenders remain visible. Heavy horizontal cancellation merges the following low letters, so the ending osons remains uncertain.

A tall looped f is followed by two separately raised i marks, with a short joining n stroke between their stems. Horizontal cancellation covers the middle height but leaves these distinguishing upper and lower remnants.
The isolated letter after E= has two compact opposing bends and a lower leftward foot. It has neither an oval sigma bowl nor a rightward top arm.
The word has low opening con strokes, a dotted i beside the slanting s, a tall d stem, and a raised accent over the following low run. A separate open curved s finishes the word.

An open c leads into a long low connector without a clear p descent, followed by a looped d-like rise and detached small ending strokes. The compressed middle and ending do not securely distinguish correspondante from considérée.
A separate hooked l and high apostrophe precede the long low uni run; the right end rises into a crossed t and has a small elevated acute stroke over the ending.
After the separate et are two low rounded opening turns, a tall oblique rise in the right half and a flat terminal tail. Those compressed strokes do not isolate the proposed l-o-r-s sequence.
A left loop with a tall d-like stem and a right arched stroke with an upright remain visible. The heavy horizontal cancellation hides the intervening o/n joins and the putative t crossbar.

The insertion contains a deep looped descender, low joined cups and a tall right stem beneath the long connector; small upper strokes overlap the neighboring main line. The connector and compressed writing prevent a secure separation of all three proposed words.

The first word has an open c, a long low connected prefix, a raised d-like loop and separated accented ending strokes. The detached following word has a low s/u run and a final rising r before the capital A.
